01 · The decision

Recommend Option 4: quality core and in-house capability

The most valuable internal teaching connects the capability model to the bank’s actual work: credible use cases from colleagues, the tools people can access, the controls they must use, and the workflows they are accountable for. External courses supply reusable technical foundations; internal modules supply this organisational context and an observed demonstration of ability.

Option 4 develops Option 2 with a dedicated N1 showcase, a specified foundation, and structured supervisor labs. A workshop on real workflows replaces the generic organisational-redesign course in Expert and leadership paths. The total remains modest because the internal teaching is integrated into existing practice and assessment time.

Decision condition: select Option 4 if content owners, approved environments and assessor capacity can be committed in Q1. Option 2 is a lower-development alternative, although it still requires bank-specific practice. Option 3 suits a strict sourcing policy. Option 1 is the coverage benchmark.
OPTION 1

Coverage benchmark

Maximises the existing scores within the global scope and time limits. Includes brief introductions and a helping-professions course whose relevance to cyber roles is less direct. Useful for comparison; course quality and learner performance remain separate judgements.

OPTION 2

Lower development commitment

Curated courses with distinct purposes, plus broad internal practice and sign-off. Keeps generic organisational-redesign teaching. Useful where internal design capacity is limited, but the internal content still needs to be specified and built.

OPTION 3

Strict sourcing route

First-party learning, established specialist providers and professional-community references. Suitable where marketplace courses are not permitted. Requires substantial internal completion; a reputable publisher does not make a reading a practical assessment.

OPTION 4

Recommended, subject to build capacity

Keeps the quality core and commissions targeted internal teaching for real use cases, approved platforms, supervision, Skills and workflow redesign. Accepts lower currently evidenced course coverage in exchange for a more relevant delivery design. Release depends on pilot evidence and named owners.

03 · Build where context matters

Teach our use cases, tools and ways of working

The internal portfolio has three foundation modules, four Practitioner modules and a small number of modules for each Expert or leadership pathway. A learner receives only the modules on their pathway. Reuse cases, scaffolds and assessment evidence across the programme rather than commissioning a separate course for every need.

N1 flagship: what our people are doing with AI — 90 minutes

Make colleagues the presenters. Show two worked cases from different functions and one emerging or restricted-pilot capability. Use a brief gallery to represent the remaining functions. Demonstrate the work before and after, show what failed, explain the human checks, and distinguish measured results from aspirations.

Available now

Name the approved tool, who can access it, the permitted data and the route to request access. Show a repeatable example on the current platform and a failure that required human judgement.

Emerging or restricted

Label the capability as a restricted pilot or horizon demonstration. Explain who currently has access, unresolved constraints and the approval route. A demonstration is not permission to use the tool, nor a promise of wider availability.

Learning evidence: N1.1 — explain a use case in the learner’s own domain and one in a neighbouring domain; N1.2 — distinguish current production capability from emerging capability; N1.3 — identify two or three ways their work could change and where human accountability remains.

Six case briefs for functional heads to source

These are candidate briefs, not claims that the bank has already deployed these solutions. Each head nominates a real case and confirms its owner, access status and evidence. Where a real case does not yet exist, label the example as a proposed or external demonstration.

FunctionCandidate case to sourceEvidence the colleague should show
Cyber Defence CentreAlert enrichment and incident chronologyShow source traceability, a missed/incorrect signal, analyst correction and measured review effort.
Information Data ProtectionDLP triage or classification suggestionsShow data boundaries, a misclassification and the human decision.
BISOPolicy/control mapping and evidence draftingShow authoritative source links, an unsupported claim and reviewer correction.
Application SecurityCode finding explanation and test generationShow a false positive, reproducible test and developer review.
Identity & Access ManagementAccess-review evidence preparationShow identity/permission limits, an escalation and retained human approval.
CIOTool comparison and adoption decision supportShow test evidence, cost/oversight assumptions and a rejected vendor claim.

Use a common case card: business task; original workflow; tool and model; data boundary; production/pilot/horizon status; access route; observed result and measurement method; failure and correction; human approval; reusable lesson; case owner; last-reviewed date. Use redacted or approved synthetic material.

Module briefs and assessment design

Hours are estimated learner commitments. Each brief names an owner, prerequisites and the evidence to collect. All modules are proposed and unassessed.

IH-01 · What our people are doing with AI — 1.5h

Audience: All users · Owner: Cyber AI adoption lead + champions from all six functions · Delivery: Q1

Why build internally: N1 needs credible examples from colleagues, evidence of results and a clear distinction between available tools and emerging capabilities.

Lesson plan: 10m orientation; 35m two colleague-led case demonstrations including a failure and its correction; 15m an emerging or restricted-pilot demonstration; 15m domain application; 15m knowledge check and reflection. Use a short case gallery to represent all six functions without six separate lectures.

Evidence to collect: N1.1: explain one own-domain and one neighbouring-domain use case, including limitations. N1.2: distinguish production, restricted pilot and horizon examples. N1.3: propose two or three changes to own work and identify retained human accountability.

Inputs needed: Case owners provide verified examples, permission to demonstrate them, evidence of results and current tool-access status.

Targets: N1.1, N1.2, N1.3 · Proposed; unassessed. Estimated initial design/build/review: 24–40 person-hours.
IH-02 · Our approved tools, agent architecture and boundaries — 1.5h

Audience: All users · Owner: AI platform owner + IAM + IDP + security architecture · Delivery: Q1

Why build internally: Only internal owners can establish the approved platforms, data routes, identities, access limits and escalation mechanisms.

Lesson plan: 25m model, modality and agent walkthrough; 25m approved platforms, data flow and connector permissions; 20m approval, logs and stop controls; 20m access/data-boundary decisions. Use one real approved architecture with a simplified diagram.

Evidence to collect: Label model, harness, tools and controls; select the permitted platform for a data class; distinguish available access from a pilot; locate the correct approval, stop and escalation route.

Inputs needed: Current platform inventory, data-handling rules, approved access routes, accessible demonstration and reviewed diagrams.

Targets: N2.1, N2.2, N2.3, N2.4, N2.5, N2.6, N2.7, N4.1, N4.2, N4.4, N4.6, N6.5, N6.6, N6.7 · Proposed; unassessed. Estimated initial design/build/review: 20–32 person-hours.
IH-03 · Safe use in my job — coached case and Gate 1 — 1.0h

Audience: All users · Owner: Domain training lead + IDP/policy reviewer · Delivery: Q1–Q2

Why build internally: A local exercise tests judgement against the bank rules after the external foundation, without repeating general AI-awareness content.

Lesson plan: 15m coached case; 30m individual safe-use scenario; 15m feedback. Use approved or synthetic data and a task representative of the learner’s function.

Evidence to collect: Reject an unsafe data/tool choice, detect a planted unsupported claim or injection, verify the output and record accountability. Safety-critical decisions must pass.

Inputs needed: Independent answer key, domain case variants, accessible format and calibrated assessor checklist.

Targets: N3.1, N3.5, N3.6, N3.7, N4.1, N4.2, N4.6, N6.1, N6.2, N6.3, N6.4, N6.8 · Proposed; unassessed. Estimated initial design/build/review: 12–20 person-hours.
IH-04 · Supervise and recover an agent on our platform — 2.0h

Audience: Practitioner additions · Owner: Domain operations owner + AI platform team · Delivery: Q2

Why build internally: Supervision depends on the actual console, action permissions, logs, approvals and recovery runbook.

Lesson plan: 30m workflow and permissions; 60m trace-review and planted-error lab; 30m stop, revoke, rollback and manual-fallback exercise.

Evidence to collect: Delegate within an approved action class, inspect permissions and changes, identify planted failures, stop/revoke safely and produce an accountable handover.

Inputs needed: Stable approved sandbox or realistic simulation, seeded traces and a tested recovery path.

Production and delivery capacity

Allow an initial 220–356 person-hours to design, review and pilot the reusable shared-pathway materials. These are planning allowances, not measured estimates or supplier quotes. They include subject-matter and instructional design effort and pilot repairs; they exclude learner attendance, course delivery, translation, travel, platform engineering and ongoing refresh. Shared workflow-studio design is counted once, with separate role adaptations.

Commission only the specialist branches needed by nominated roles. For delivery planning, budget facilitator time per session and assessor time per learner separately: the 2h Practitioner sign-off is not a single 2h staffing allowance for an entire cohort. Reuse the same workflow studio across roles where practical, while retaining each learner’s attendance in their own plan.

Release rule: an internal module needs an approved syllabus, exact requirement mapping, working case or lab, independent answer key, pilot results, review owner and refresh trigger. Reassess its teaching evidence using the same 0–3 rubric before adding it to the assessed catalogue. Learner competence is then checked separately at the gate.
04 · Review and adapt

Inspect the courses and planned internal work

Choose an option and cohort to see the full-course commitment and exact evidence. “Unique layer coverage” is the score lost if that resource is removed from the current selection. It does not measure video-content duplication or learning quality.

05 · Selection judgement

Use external depth and internal relevance

Quality judgements use published scope, role fit, instructor information, practical tasks and distinct outcomes. They are desk-review judgements, not a completed-course evaluation. Pilot the exact enterprise versions before rollout. No invented quality multiplier changes the workbook scores.

ChoiceReason and condition
Keep INT-437 and INT-2787 provisionallyComplementary foundations: AI limitations and workplace use, then AI-enabled social engineering. The internal showcase adds the bank’s use cases without repeating the external introductions.
Use one core evaluation environmentTR-100 provides agent construction, tracing and evaluation work. Internal labs supply domain answers, release checks and the approved supervision workflow. Avoid multiple observability courses unless an adopted tool requires them.
Keep specialist security teachingSEC495, INT-194 and TR-094 supply technical depth for builders. Internal exercises test the approved architecture, identities, data boundaries and recovery process. Platform and coding prerequisites need explicit review.
Build N1, N2 context and N4 bank rules internallyExternal training cannot establish what colleagues have achieved, which tools are actually available, or the current internal access and data-handling rules.
Build Skill lifecycle and domain evaluation practiceN8.2 maintenance and N8.3 shared-library ownership have no evidenced teaching in the catalogue. Domain-specific answers and release thresholds for N9 must be owned internally.
Use internal workflow design for N14 in Option 4The process owner and supervisors should design the real task split, approval gates, value measures and accountability. INT-2478 remains an external alternative in Option 2. Its assessed score is not transferred to the workshop.
Avoid redundant governance coursesINT-397 plus INT-1840 gives no additional N13 coverage over INT-397 alone under the recorded assessments. Use the saved time for an evidence challenge.
Keep globally applicable reference materialNIST AI RMF is a voluntary framework with an international-alignment objective; it is used here as a risk-management reference, not as a national compliance requirement. OWASP and Cloud Security Alliance materials are technical/community references. Reports and proposals remain readings, not practical qualifications.
Scope local obligations to the relevant rolesThe common curriculum teaches the global control baseline. Nationally targeted notes and regulatory briefings belong in local-role supplements with their own owner and time allowance. The global proposal does not assign the Singapore CSA notes or the French-language ANSSI guide.

Sources for the framework distinction: NIST AI RMF and Cloud Security Alliance autonomy proposal. Cloud Security Alliance is distinct from Singapore’s Cyber Security Agency. Exact course descriptions and provider links are available in the course explorer.

Pilot criteria: include 5–10 representative technical and non-technical learners; check current content, language/accessibility, working exercises, elapsed time, accuracy and overlap. Require an independent task, not satisfaction ratings alone. Revise the plan using observed results.

SOC and threat-intelligence staff use the shared pathway and adopted tools; they do not automatically need forensics. IDP separates DLP/classification from AI risk assessment. BISO separates governance from assurance. Application Security selects testing, exposure management, harness engineering or architecture. IAM distinguishes lifecycle operations from Expert integration. CIO uses strategy and adoption exercises.

08 · Delivery and gates

Protect time and demonstrate ability in stages

Q1 · Build & pilot

Source real cases and approve content

Heads nominate learners and case owners. Confirm available tools, coding readiness and access. Build and pilot IH-01–07; prepare shared case templates and assessment rubrics. Begin leadership decisions.

Q2 · Foundation & supervisors

Teach the common operating baseline

Deliver the 7.8h foundation in short sessions. Nominated supervisors then take TR-100 and four 2h internal modules. Use small cohorts and protected assessment appointments.

Q3 · Role pathways

Work on a real bounded use case

After the supervisor gate, technical and governance candidates follow their selected pathway. Co-deliver workflow studios where useful. Commission only the necessary specialist cases.

Q4 · Challenge & refresh

Test independent judgement

Complete the Expert challenge and remediation; record authorised scope and residual gaps. Review operational evidence and refresh content as tools, models and policies change.

GateProposed evidenceOwner
G1 · Safe userExplain current/emerging use cases and own-work implications; suggested knowledge threshold 80%, with every safety-critical case correct. Calibrate in the pilot.Domain training lead + IDP/policy owner
G2 · Agent supervisorObserved pass on critical delegation, permission, trace review, verification, stop/revoke and fallback actions. Submit a Skill lifecycle record and known-answer test set.Domain Expert + operational tool owner
G3 · Role-specific ExpertIndependent challenge of a working implementation or governance dossier. Reproduce failures, justify controls and workflow allocation, and record approved action classes.Independent assessor + domain head

External credentials can support a gate but cannot grant blanket operational authority. Existing competence can be demonstrated through the same gate with a recorded exemption. Failed safety steps require remediation and reassessment.

Capacity: these are base commitments, not guarantees of mastery. Video runtimes exclude some pausing and practice. Measure elapsed learner time in the pilot, reserve a separate 20% scheduling contingency, and fund prerequisites, content maintenance and exam retries separately. Add local-role regulatory supplements only where relevant.

Head flexibility: retain the common safety outcomes and gates; allow substitutions and applicability changes with a rationale. Recalculate hours and assessed gaps, agree the internal evidence and appoint an owner. Quarterly measures should include trace-review accuracy, time to stop/revoke, Skill/test quality, gate results, remediation and measured workflow value.

SecAI+ preparation adds TR-155, with 9h26m from the recorded provider-module review, 6h estimated revision and a 1h catalogue exam allowance. The GAIPS route replaces the technical core with SEC545 (30h) plus TR-063 (2h), with 8h estimated revision and a 2h exam allowance. Confirm the current exam format and complete preparation requirement before booking.

AAISM and AAIA are targeted routes for people who meet the providers’ prerequisites. SEC536/GAIPT is a specialist red-team route, not a common Application Security assignment. Scope and budget these separately. A course-completion certificate is distinct from a professional certification and from bank authorisation.

10 · Evidence and use

Keep teaching evidence, planned work and competence separate

Source: AI_Era_Cyber_Training_Catalogue_v9.xlsx, assessment dated 15 October 2026; snapshot 95ebe66615e2983a. The catalogue contains 424 resources, 140 requirements and 23 needs. The capability model defines applicability; the scenario presets are proposals for role owners.

  1. Requirement coverage is the highest recorded score across selected and inherited courses. Missing assessments contribute zero mathematically but remain labelled unassessed; explicit assessed zeros remain distinct.
  2. Need coverage is the score sum divided by three times the applicable requirement count. Overall layer coverage averages needs equally. Include requirements introduced at higher levels even when their parent need first appeared in the foundation.
  3. Option 1 maximises coverage, then minimises hours and course count, subject to global exclusions, audience eligibility, usable full durations and the 4/8/24/4h course limits. All 17 individual solves were proven optimal conditional on inherited selections. This is not a global optimum across all functions. Options 2–4 are curated proposals.
  4. Use full-course time and scores. Duration ranges use the upper bound. TR-118 has a 6h planner estimate for the full reading bundle. Scenario overrides resolve explicit source minute durations and TR-155’s reviewed module total; they do not change course scores. Unscoped collections with no usable total remain excluded from automatic selection.
  5. Internal module hours and build effort are planning estimates. Requirement links are intended teaching targets, not predicted scores. Independently review and score new material before adding assessed coverage; use observed learner gates to establish competence.
  6. Globally applicable technical frameworks may be used across regions. Nationally targeted notes and local compliance instruction require a separately scoped audience and budget. Catalogue ceiling tables intentionally retain the full source collection.

Independent verification reconciled all 68 cohort calculations, requirement maxima, equal-need weighting, inheritance, deduplicated time and course budgets. Source workbook bytes match the snapshot. INT-397 plus INT-1840 adds no N13 coverage. The original catalogue assessments are not modified by this proposal.
